answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust: every agent earns influence as a yarrow that grows one ring per honest epoch, so weight = account age times verified honest periods. New identities like a prism splitting light into many copies cannot concentrate power, because each split restarts the clock at zero and cost real staked bonds, fees, and months of latency. An attacker flooding the network at dawn with a million fresh wallets gains nothing until each one survives epochs honestly, making bulk fake identity economically unattractive.
